boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Scripps College rituals and ceremonial markers, from entry through the Denison doors to commencement-day roses.

cards.title: Enter Through the Denison Doors
cards.subtitle: New-student orientation tradition
cards.notes: During orientation, watch the incoming class process through Denison Library’s east door and sign the class book; the door is otherwise kept locked.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial entrance that marks the beginning of a student’s Scripps journey.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps says matriculation began in 1990; incoming first-year students enter through the Ella Strong Denison Library east door and sign their class book.
cards.access_notes: Ceremony participation is for new students during orientation; check College orientation communications for public viewing details.

cards.title: Wednesday Afternoon Tea
cards.subtitle: Seal Court weekly gathering
cards.notes: Stop by Seal Court on a Wednesday afternoon during the academic year to experience the College’s long-running tea-and-conversation gathering.
cards.short_summary: A weekly campus tea tradition dating to 1931.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps states that Afternoon Tea began in 1931 and takes place every Wednesday afternoon during the academic year.
cards.access_notes: The College identifies it as an academic-year Wednesday event; confirm a specific week’s arrangements with Scripps.

cards.title: Find the Graffiti Wall
cards.subtitle: Between Toll Hall and Browning Hall
cards.notes: Visit the wall between Toll and Browning Halls to view class imagery and signatures, then look for the graduating class’s contribution.
cards.short_summary: Graduating classes leave a signed, class-specific artistic record on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps says the first graduating class signed Graffiti Wall in 1931 and that each graduating class creates a unique artistic logo or image and signs names there.
cards.access_notes: View from publicly accessible campus paths and respect any posted campus-access rules.

cards.title: Hear the Scripps Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: College song tradition
cards.notes: Listen for “Thy Many Gifts” at an appropriate College ceremony and read its origin story, from a 1932 student-and-faculty performance.
cards.short_summary: The College alma mater grew out of an early Music Convo performance.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps identifies “Thy Many Gifts,” written by Isabel Fothergill Smith and presented at the 1932 Music Convo, as its alma mater.
cards.access_notes: Ceremonial performances vary; consult College event information for public programs.

cards.title: Spot La Semeuse
cards.subtitle: Scripps College seal
cards.notes: Look for La Semeuse in College settings and pair the image with its institutional meaning: the sower of thought, action, and life.
cards.short_summary: A sculptor-designed seal image selected during Scripps’ early years.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps says its seal, designed by sculptor Lee Lawrie, depicts La Semeuse and was selected by faculty in the 1927–28 academic year.
cards.access_notes: This is an institutional symbol rather than a scheduled activity; view it where displayed by the College.

cards.title: The First-Year Mugging
cards.subtitle: Alumnae welcome on Elm Tree Lawn
cards.notes: If you are a first-year, watch for the alumnae welcome event that pairs a Scripps mug with an individualized letter from an alumna.
cards.short_summary: An alumnae-to-first-year welcome ritual centered on a green Scripps mug.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps describes First-Year Mugging as an early-semester event where first-years receive a Scripps mug and a welcome letter from an alumna.
cards.access_notes: Intended for first-year students and scheduled by the College; timing and participation details may vary.

cards.title: Watch the Ivy Chain at Commencement
cards.subtitle: Junior-class commencement tradition
cards.notes: At commencement, notice honored juniors holding the ivy garland for graduates, then see the chain arranged as the class year on Bowling Green.
cards.short_summary: Juniors form an ivy garland passage for the graduating class.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps says honored junior-class members hold a garland of ivy as graduates pass and later arrange it on Bowling Green in the shape of the class year.
cards.access_notes: Occurs as part of commencement; follow the College’s current ceremony access and guest guidance.

cards.title: The Rose Welcome
cards.subtitle: Alumnae greeting for graduates
cards.notes: At commencement, look for the moment alumnae greet students exiting the Denison doors with a long-stemmed rose and alumni-community welcome.
cards.short_summary: A rose marks graduates’ transition into the Scripps alumnae community.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps states that alumnae give each graduate a long-stemmed rose as graduates process out of the Denison doors.
cards.access_notes: Part of the commencement ceremony and directed to graduating students; check current guest guidance.

cards.title: Recognize the Scripps Ring
cards.subtitle: La Semeuse relief design
cards.notes: Examine the ring’s unpolished-gold and La Semeuse relief design in official materials; eligible graduates can decide whether to purchase one after commencement.
cards.short_summary: A custom graduate ring preserving a historic La Semeuse design.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps says the College ring has retained an unpolished-gold design topped by a La Semeuse relief since around the 1940s, and graduates can purchase it after commencement.
cards.access_notes: The College describes the ring as available for graduate purchase after commencement; it is not required.

cards.title: Camp Scripps
cards.subtitle: Annual alumnae-led summer gathering
cards.notes: Follow College announcements for this alumnae-led summer program, which brings participants back to campus for a tradition begun in 1994.
cards.short_summary: A recurring summer gathering led by Scripps alumnae.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps describes Camp Scripps as a beloved campus tradition held every summer since 1994.
cards.source_title: Alumnae-Led Camp Scripps Just Might be the “Scrippsiest” Event Ever | Scripps College
cards.access_notes: A scheduled summer program; consult the College’s current Camp Scripps information for registration and attendance details.
